Merged and verified on `main`.

## Landed

[#1029](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1029) squash-merged as `4c482f6`, closing [#1022](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1022). Post-merge on `main`: **2143 tests passing**, `check_the_world` 0 blocking. `packs/core/` and `packs/grow_with_claudinite/` are gone; [`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`](packs/claudinite-lifecycle/README.md) and [`packs/claudinite-growth/`](packs/claudinite-growth/README.md) are in their place, with the scheduled-task contract in the second.

Conversation captured to `conversation-logs` (1141 entries) for the growth pack to mine later.

## Folders this touched

- **`engine/pack_loader/`** — new `renamed-packs.mjs`, the legacy-id map; `pack-registry.mjs` canonicalizes both a declared id and a mounted `pack.mjs`'s own id.
- **`engine/migrations/2026-08-19-pack-renames/`** — new record: moves each member's mount directories, rewrites its declaration under narrow anchors.
- **`engine/`** — `ENGINE_VERSION` 4→5 (what puts the record in every member's gap), `RELEASES.md` row, `checks/helpers/active-migrations.mjs` canonicalizes stamped `packVersions` keys, `scheduler/queue/work-item.mjs` canonicalizes a stored work-item title.
- **`updates/`** — `pack-update.mjs` and `install.mjs` read the stamp raw, so both canonicalize before planning.
- **`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`, `packs/claudinite-growth/`** — the renames, and the contract's move between them.
- **`packs/sheepdog/`, `packs/basics/`** — version bumps and link repointing.
- **`.claudinite-checks.json`** — two reviewed barrier exceptions plus `engine/migrations` as a structural carve-out.

## Worth knowing

Engine version 5 is now released, so **the record reaches the fleet on each member's next converge** — that's the fleet-wide effect, and it's live. The loader tolerance means a member is safe whichever half lands first, and it retires when no member's declaration or stamp still carries an old spelling — read off the fleet, not a calendar.

One thing that nearly went wrong and is worth remembering: the first canary run qualified the pre-rebase tree, and three commits landed under it. Merging on that row would have recorded a rehearsal that never saw this code — the exact vacuous-gate failure the marker assertion exists to catch. The re-run's step 7 passed rather than skipping, so this one is real.

> ✅ All done — merged, `main` green, capture pushed, branch pruned.

=== dispatch inputs ===
# `workflow_dispatch` is not a convenience: it is the never-wait-for-the-cron
# lever every forced run, migration and validation burst depends on. Its one
# input is how that lever reaches ACROSS repos: the fleet enforcer dispatches
# this workflow naming the tasks to run now, and this member wakes its own
# standing items with its own token (DESIGN §8). The alternative — the enforcer
# editing every member's issues directly — would widen the fleet PAT to issue
# writes on every repository, for a job the member can do for itself.
name: Claudinite scheduler

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '12 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      wake:
        description: 'Task ids to run now (`pack/task` or a bare task name, space-separated) — wakes each one’s standing item regardless of its anchor'
        required: false
        type: string

# One tick at a time, always. The tick's duplicate-standing-item self-heal is
# written assuming exactly this — it closes every open family item but the oldest,
# which is safe precisely because two ticks never run at once.
concurrency:
  group: claudinite-tick
  cancel-in-progress: false

input.body:
Found by forcing the canary to update against engine 5 (#1022, #1029) and reading its artifacts back.

## What happened

Everything converged except the one thing the record exists for. On `missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary` after the forced run ([PR 121](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/121)):

- `engineVersion` 4 → 5 ✅
- `packVersions` keys renamed — `claudinite-lifecycle: 8`, `claudinite-growth: 7`, old keys gone ✅
- mount directories moved — `packs/core/` and `packs/grow_with_claudinite/` gone, renamed trees present, `pack.mjs` announcing the new ids ✅
- **`packs` array still reads `"core"` and `"grow_with_claudinite"`** ❌

## Why

The record's bare-element pattern anchors on the packs array:

```
/("packs"\s*:\s*\[(?:[^\]]*?,)?\s*)"core"(\s*[,\]])/g
```

`[^\]]*?` cannot cross a `]`. A real declaration's packs array holds entry objects with nested arrays:

```json
"packs": [
  "basics",
  { "id": "barriers", "via": [ "basics" ] },
  { "id": "git-github", "via": [ "basics" ] },
  "grow_with_claudinite",
  ...
  "core"
]
```

Both target elements sit *after* those nested `]`, so the anchor never reaches them.

The test fixture used an entry object with a plain `config` and no nested array — it spelled the same gap the pattern had. A fixture can only prove the matching; it can never disagree with you. The real-tree replay would have caught it in one call.

## Impact

Bounded, and only because the tolerance was built first: the loader resolves both spellings, so the canary read `core` → `claudinite-lifecycle` correctly and updated *from version 6* rather than reinstalling at latest. Nothing is broken in any member. What is lost is convergence — the declarations never move to the new spelling, so `renamed-packs.mjs` can never be retired, which was the entire point of shipping a record beside it.

## Fix

Replace the regex with a **structural** op, the shape `normalizeLocalDeclarations` already has: parse the declaration, rewrite ids in the `packs` array only, preserve entry objects, config, answers and order, idempotent. Driven by `RENAMED_PACKS` so no future rename has to restate ids in a record. A structural op also retires the false-positive risk the narrow regex was defending against — a member's own `{ "from": "core" }` barrier rule is not in the `packs` array and is never seen.

Needs its own record at **engine 6**: `migrationApplies` is `want > have`, so the v5 record can never re-apply to a member already stamped 5 — the canary among them.

Tested against a **real** member declaration, not only a synthetic one.

The record's declaration rewrite converged nothing. core → claudinite-lifecycle and grow_with_claudinite → claudinite-growth

The scheduled-task authoring contract moves with the rename: scheduled-tasks.md
and its four checks judge whether a task is WRITTEN correctly, which is authoring,
not whether Claudinite is working in the repo — so they land in the growth pack
beside the rest of the authoring surface, and the lifecycle pack keeps only the
rules that answer for a member's own Claudinite status.

Activation matches a declared id literally, so the rename's real hazard is a
member whose declaration and mount disagree: it does not get a degraded pack, it
gets none — and for the pack carrying `update` that is unrecoverable, because the
machinery that would deliver the repair is the machinery that went missing.
engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs closes every such window by resolving both
spellings at the loader, on the declared id, the stamped packVersions key, a work
item's stored title, and a mounted pack.mjs still announcing its old id. The
migration record then converges the declaration and moves the mount directories,
so the tolerance can one day be retired — but nothing depends on it having run.

half that never landed: the mount directories moved and the stamped packVersions

The record rewrote it textually, anchored on "packs": [ so a member's own
{ "from": "core" } barrier rule could never be caught by accident. That anchor
cannot cross a ']', and a real packs array holds entry objects with nested arrays
— { "id": "barriers", "via": ["basics"] } — so every element after the first
such object was invisible to it. The fixture had an entry object with a plain
config and no nesting: it spelled the same gap the pattern had, and agreed.

applyPackRenames parses instead, reads only the packs array, and takes its ids
from the engine's rename map, so a future rename needs no new op. Parsing also
retires the false-positive the anchor existed to prevent — a barrier rule is not
in the packs array and is never seen.

A separate record at engine 6 rather than a repair of the 5 one: a record applies
only while a repo sits below its version, so the 5 record can never run again on
a member already stamped 5 — which is precisely the member still needing it.

core → claudinite-lifecycle and grow_with_claudinite → claudinite-growth

The scheduled-task authoring contract moves with the rename: scheduled-tasks.md
and its four checks judge whether a task is WRITTEN correctly, which is authoring,
not whether Claudinite is working in the repo — so they land in the growth pack
beside the rest of the authoring surface, and the lifecycle pack keeps only the
rules that answer for a member's own Claudinite status.

Activation matches a declared id literally, so the rename's real hazard is a
member whose declaration and mount disagree: it does not get a degraded pack, it
gets none — and for the pack carrying `update` that is unrecoverable, because the
machinery that would deliver the repair is the machinery that went missing.
engine/pack_loader/renamed-packs.mjs closes every such window by resolving both
spellings at the loader, on the declared id, the stamped packVersions key, a work
item's stored title, and a mounted pack.mjs still announcing its old id. The
migration record then converges the declaration and moves the mount directories,
so the tolerance can one day be retired — but nothing depends on it having run.

input.body:
Closes #1041.

Found by forcing `missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary` to update against engine 5 and reading its artifacts back, rather than by trusting the run's exit code.

## What the forced run showed

Three of four halves converged. The fourth — the one the record exists for — did nothing.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `engineVersion` | 4 | 5 ✅ |
| `packVersions` | `core: 6`, `grow_with_claudinite: 6` | `claudinite-lifecycle: 8`, `claudinite-growth: 7` ✅ |
| mount dirs | `packs/core/`, `packs/grow_with_claudinite/` | renamed, old gone, `pack.mjs` on the new ids ✅ |
| `packs` array | `"core"`, `"grow_with_claudinite"` | **unchanged** ❌ |

## Why it did nothing

The record rewrote the declaration textually, anchored on `"packs": [` so a member's own `{ "from": "core" }` barrier rule could never be caught by accident:

```
/("packs"\s*:\s*\[(?:[^\]]*?,)?\s*)"core"(\s*[,\]])/g
```

`[^\]]*?` cannot cross a `]`, and a real packs array holds entry objects with nested arrays:

```json
"packs": [
  "basics",
  { "id": "barriers", "via": [ "basics" ] },
  { "id": "git-github", "via": [ "basics" ] },
  "grow_with_claudinite",
  ...
  "core"
]
```

Both targets sit after those nested `]`. The anchor never reached them.

The fixture used an entry object with a plain `config` and no nesting — it spelled the same gap the pattern had, so it agreed. A fixture written from the same understanding as the code can only prove the matching; a real-tree replay is the only thing that can disagree.

## The fix

`applyPackRenames` — structural, the shape `normalizeLocalDeclarations` already has. It parses, rewrites ids in the `packs` array only, preserves entry objects, config, `answers`, `via` and order, skips local declarations, and is idempotent. Ids come from the engine's own `RENAMED_PACKS`, so a future rename needs no new op and no record restating them.

Parsing also retires the false-positive the anchor existed to prevent: a barrier rule isn't in the `packs` array, so it is never seen. The narrow regex is removed from the version 5 record rather than repaired — a member already stamped 5 never runs it again, so a fix there would reach only the repos that were never affected.

**A separate record at engine 6** for that same reason: `migrationApplies` is `want > have`, so version 5's record can never re-run on a member stamped 5 — which is exactly the member whose declaration still needs moving. Nothing depends on either record having run; the loader tolerance means a member reads correctly either way. What this buys is the day `renamed-packs.mjs` can be retired.

## Impact of the original bug

None to any member, and only because the tolerance was built first — the canary read `core` → `claudinite-lifecycle` throughout, which is why its update was `claudinite-lifecycle 6 → 8` (an update from the version stamped under the old key) rather than a reinstall at latest. What was lost was convergence, and with it the ability to ever retire the aliases.

## Verification

- Test fixture is now **the canary's real pre-rename declaration** (`engine-tests/fixtures/member-declaration-pre-rename.json`), captured before it converged.
- Both new assertions watched failing against the old anchor's behaviour before the structural op went in.
- Full suite **2145 passing**; `check_the_world` 0 blocking; `check_the_work` exits 0.
- Engine 6 qualified by canary rehearsal [run 32270294377](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/actions/runs/32270294377) against this head.

Canary PR [121](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/pull/121) is open and untouched — it is the member's own delivery, and re-forcing after this lands is what will confirm the declaration converges.

- **`engine/migrations/`** — new `applyPackRenames` op in `registry.mjs` (structural, driven by `RENAMED_PACKS`), wired into `applyMigration`; new `2026-08-19-pack-renames-declaration/` record at version 6; the broken textual rewrite removed from the version 5 record.

The forced update did what you asked for, and the answer was **partly no**. Engine version, pack versions and the whole mount converged; the `packs` array didn't, because my record's regex couldn't cross a nested array inside an entry object. My fixture had no nesting, so it confirmed the bug rather than catching it.

Two things kept that from being serious. The loader tolerance meant no member broke — the canary read `core` correctly and updated *from* version 6 rather than reinstalling at latest, which is itself the cleanest evidence the tolerance works. And forcing a real member is what surfaced it; the run's own exit code said success.

Once it lands I'll force the canary again to confirm the `packs` array actually converges, which is the assertion this whole detour exists to make.
